note: In-session run, published Sat 8 Aug covering the Friday 7 Aug closes (markets shut for the weekend). 34 items gathered across four finders, every one re-opened and verified; none dropped. Where finders disagreed on a figure — silver, Fed odds, the 10Y and oil — the reconciled value is used and the discrepancy stated in the item rather than averaged away. The headless CLI has been logged out since 4 Aug; this run replaces it.

items.headline: US July payrolls CONTRACT 23,000 vs ~+80,000 expected — and May/June revised down 103,000
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls FELL 23,000 in July against consensus of roughly +80,000 to +83,000, the first outright decline in months. May was cut from 129,000 to 63,000 and June from 57,000 to 20,000 — 103,000 of downward revisions combined. Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, but for a bad reason: 264,000 left the labour force and participation dropped to 61.4%, a near 5.5-year low. Wage growth slowed to +3.2% y/y from +3.4%. Losses led by leisure/hospitality (-40,000) and local government education (-50,000). NOTE: bls.gov returns HTTP 403, so these are from document-level press coverage that reconciles across Reuters/Forbes/Quartz, not the BLS release itself.
items.actionable: The most important input for your book this week. A contracting labour market with cooling wages removes the Fed's justification for the September hike — directly dovish for your levered silver and the miners. But read the falling unemployment rate as cosmetic: it fell because people stopped looking, not because anyone got hired. The revisions matter more than the headline — four months of apparent "stabilisation" were an illusion.

items.headline: September Fed hike odds collapse to ~40-44%, from ~55-58% before the report — no longer the base case
items.summary: Fed funds futures repriced hard. Sources put the post-release hike probability between 40% and 44% (Reuters 44% from 57%; Yahoo 40% from 55%; CME hold probability 56%, implying ~44% hike). The range reflects different snapshot times through the session; all agree a September hike ceased to be the base case.
items.actionable: A regime shift from where your dashboard stood on 6 Aug, when September was priced ~65% for a HIKE. For a 1.6x levered silver position on IBKR margin this is a double benefit — less real-rate pressure on the metal AND a cap on your financing cost. The risk is a violent reversal on the 12 Aug CPI print, especially with ISM Services prices at 70.3.

items.headline: Silver rips to $63.54 (+3.3%), intraday high $65.05; gold $4,343.43 (+2.4%), a two-month high
items.summary: Silver closed $63.54, up 3.32% (+$2.04), with an intraday high of $65.05 — a seven-week high. Gold closed $4,343.43, +2.44% (+$103.58), a two-month high, with futures printing $4,411.70 intraday. One source (Fortune) reported silver around $64.3 / +4.1%; the $63.54 close is corroborated by three separate readings and is used here, with the discrepancy noted rather than averaged.
items.actionable: Your single largest risk is now working hard. Silver has gone from ~$55.6 in late July to $63.54 — roughly +14% — and is far above the $60 level that was the concern. At 1.6x leverage that is a substantial equity gain in the IBKR account. Consider whether the position size you set for a falling market is still the one you want in a rising one.

items.headline: Gold miners go vertical: GDX +7.10% to $89.88, capping a 20%-plus week
items.summary: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF rose 7.10% on Friday to $89.88, completing a gain of more than 20% on the week as the Fed repricing drove leveraged exposure to the metal.
items.actionable: Direct read-through to your GDX, SILJ and SLVP holdings, which had been among the worst performers on the dashboard's trend alerts. A 20% week does not undo a 38% drawdown from the 52-week high, but it is the first genuine trend reversal signal in this sleeve since June.

items.headline: S&P 500 closes at a RECORD 7,757.64 (+0.62%); best week since April
items.summary: S&P 500 7,757.64, +47.68 (+0.62%), taking out the 7,736.52 record set on 4 August. Nasdaq 26,690.62, +1.30%. Dow 54,036.93, +0.28%. Russell 2000 3,034.49, +1.10%. On the week: Nasdaq +5.2%, S&P +3.6% (strongest since April), Dow +3.0%. Palantir +10.3%.
items.actionable: Small caps outpacing the Dow says the rally is driven by the no-hike read rather than mega-cap concentration — a healthier mix. Constructive setup for Monday's Asia open, which matters for your HK tech and SGX names after a weak Friday in Asia.

items.headline: The long end refuses to rally: 10Y only ~4.61-4.65%, 30Y 5.20%
items.summary: The 10-year eased to roughly 4.61-4.65% depending on snapshot time (down ~3bp) and the 30-year to 5.20%, down 2.6bp. A payrolls contraction plus 103,000 of downward revisions would normally drive a far larger duration rally; a sub-3bp move is the story.
items.actionable: The most important caveat to the bullish week. The bond market is still pricing an inflation problem — consistent with ISM Services prices at 70.3 — which warns the equity and metals reaction may be running ahead of what fixed income will validate. A 30Y stuck above 5% keeps the pressure on Keppel REIT and Mapletree.

items.headline: OCBC Q2 profit +22% to a record S$2.22b — first ever quarter above S$2b — and raises loan guidance
items.summary: OCBC reported Q2 net profit up 22% to S$2.22b, its first quarter above S$2b, and raised its loan growth guidance.
items.actionable: With DBS (record S$3.08b, guidance raised) this completes a strong SG bank season. Your Singapore bank exposure is delivering fundamentally, and it remains the natural hedge against the rate path that threatens the metals sleeve.

items.headline: UOB Q2 +10% to S$1.48b and lifts the dividend — but CUTS 2026 fee income guidance
items.summary: UOB posted Q2 net profit up 10% to S$1.48b and raised its dividend, while cutting its 2026 fee income guidance to low single-digit growth.
items.actionable: The one blemish in an otherwise strong SG bank season — a fee-income guidance cut against a raised dividend. Not a holding of yours directly, but it tempers the read-across from DBS and OCBC.

items.headline: Straits Times Index +1.05% to 5,698.43 — back within 15 points of its all-time high
items.summary: The STI rose 1.05% to 5,698.43 on Friday, leaving it roughly 15 points below its record.
items.actionable: Your largest regional exposure is at record levels on the back of the bank results. Note the Fund Flows tab still shows institutions net SELLERS into retail buying — a distribution pattern at record highs argues against adding here.

items.headline: China July trade beats hard: exports +23.9% y/y, imports +27.5%, surplus $112.5bn
items.summary: China reported July exports up 23.9% year-on-year in USD terms and imports up 27.5%, producing a trade surplus of $112.5bn — comfortably ahead of forecasts.
items.actionable: A genuinely strong print that supports the China reflation case behind your HK tech sleeve, and helps explain Shanghai's +2.81% week.

items.headline: Hang Seng rescued by a late bid to 25,668.03 (+0.54%); Shanghai +1.02% to a three-week high
items.summary: The Hang Seng closed +0.54% at 25,668.03 after a late bid, with SMIC +2.4%, Xiaomi +0.7% and Tencent flat. The Shanghai Composite rose 1.02% to 3,940, a three-week high, and +2.81% on the week.
items.actionable: Your HK names stabilised after the mid-week retreat, with SMIC leading. But southbound Connect flows have been selling for six straight sessions on the Fund Flows tab — the mainland bid that supported HK in July has not returned.

items.headline: Korea did NOT stabilise: KOSPI -0.60% to 6,259, second straight loss, SK Hynix -5.22%
items.summary: The KOSPI fell a further 0.60% to 6,259 after Thursday's 4.58% crash, with SK Hynix down another 5.22%.
items.actionable: The AI/memory unwind is not over. Relevant as a leading indicator for the semiconductor complex and for SMIC in your HK sleeve.

items.headline: Oil ends a brutal week: Brent settled ~$83.55 (+1.3% on the day, -7% on the week), WTI ~$78.2
items.summary: Brent settled around $83.55, up roughly 1.3% on the day but down more than 7% on the week; WTI around $78.20. Sources differ on the intraday direction — one reading had WTI at $77.08 (-0.27%) — reflecting different snapshot times; the settle prices are used here. The Hormuz situation remains unresolved.
items.actionable: Oil is down sharply on the week but bounced Friday — the Hormuz de-escalation is still only half-delivered, so the inflation tail is not gone. That is the main threat to the dovish Fed repricing driving your metals.

items.headline: MP Materials Q2: revenue +89% to $108.5m, NdPr sales more than double, new gadolinium defence offtake
items.summary: MP Materials reported Q2 revenue up 89% to $108.5m as NdPr sales more than doubled, with the net loss narrowing to $20.3m including $17.6m from the DoD arrangement, and signed a gadolinium offtake agreement.
items.actionable: The rare-earth thesis is delivering operationally even where price action has lagged — revenue +89% with the DoD price floor contributing. Relevant to the watchlist rather than a holding.
